questions.question: Q: What is the difference between unison and canon?
questions.correctAnswer: In unison, all dancers move at the same time; in canon, dancers start the same phrase at different times in sequence.

questions.question: Q: Describe how accumulation works as a choreographic device.
questions.correctAnswer: Accumulation starts with one movement, then adds a second so both are performed, then a third, and so on — the phrase gradually grows longer with each repetition.

questions.question: Q: Why might a choreographer use retrograde in a dance?
questions.correctAnswer: Retrograde creates a striking visual effect, like rewinding time. It can symbolise memory, returning to the past, or give a phrase a surprising twist that maintains audience interest.

questions.question: Q: How does repetition help communicate choreographic intention?
questions.correctAnswer: Repetition draws attention to key movements, making them memorable and emphasising their importance to the audience, reinforcing the meaning the choreographer wants to convey.

questions.question: Q: Explain how fragmentation can be used to develop a dance phrase.
questions.correctAnswer: Fragmentation breaks an existing phrase into smaller parts — these fragments can be rearranged, performed in a different order, or isolated to create new material while keeping a link to the original.
